channel.title: videos on Loud Legends
channel.description: Recent content in videos on Loud Legends

item.title: DIMMU BORGIR Announces New Guitarist Kjell Åge “Damage” Karlsen Ahead of Tons of Rock Festival
item.description: Norwegian metal band Dimmu Borgir has a new guitarist. The group announced that Kjell Åge “Damage” Karlsen has joined their lineup. He played his first show with the band on June 27 at the Tons of Rock festival in Oslo, Norway (watch it below).

item.title: AC/DC Opens European Tour in Prague, Czech President Attends; VIDEOS
item.description: AC/DC launched the summer leg of their “Power Up” European tour Thursday night in Prague, Czech Republic. The concert took place at Letiště Praha Letňany and drew an estimated crowd of 60,000 people.

item.title: KORN’s Full PINKPOP 2007 Performance With SLIPKNOT’s JOEY JORDISON Released On YouTube
item.description: A professionally filmed video of KORN’s full set at the Pinkpop Festival in the Netherlands — recorded on May 28, 2007 — has been made available online via the Pinkpop Archive YouTube channel.

item.title: GENE HOGLAN Says METALLICA’s 'One' Echoes DARK ANGEL: 'That Beat Came From Us'
item.description: In a recent interview, Gene Hoglan, drummer for the thrash metal band Dark Angel, shared his thoughts on a long-standing theory among metal fans, that Metallica’s 1988 track “One” was inspired by Dark Angel’s 1986 song “Darkness Descends.

item.title: LARS ULRICH Breaks Down the Goal of New METALLICA Doc: 'Turn The Spotlight Away From Us And Celebrate The Fans'
item.description: Metallica’s Lars Ulrich wants people to know the band isn’t the main focus of their new documentary. The real stars, he says, are the fans. Speaking on the red carpet at the Tribeca Festival premiere of Metallica Saved My Life, Ulrich explained why the film shifts attention away from the band and onto the people who have supported them for more than four decades.

item.title: OZZY OSBOURNE Says He Wants To Work With PAUL MCCARTNEY: 'I Would Be Honoured'
item.description: During a new episode of Ozzy Speaks on SiriusXM (transcribed by LOUDLEGENDS.COM), Ozzy Osbourne mentioned that he would like to collaborate with Paul McCartney. The rock icon discussed the idea while chatting with his co-host, Billy Morrison.

item.title: Dream Theater's MIKE PORTNOY Defends LARS ULRICH: 'He Takes a Beating, But He's Invaluable'
item.description: Mike Portnoy, drummer for Dream Theater, says Lars Ulrich deserves more credit. In a recent chat with El Estepario Siberiano (transcribed by LOUDLEGENDS.COM), Portnoy explained why he thinks the Metallica co-founder is often misunderstood.

item.title: WOLFGANG VAN HALEN Explains Why He Backed Out of OZZY OSBOURNE’s Final Concert: 'I Wouldn’t Be Able To Pull It Off'
item.description: Wolfgang Van Halen, son of late guitar legend Eddie Van Halen, was originally scheduled to appear at Ozzy Osbourne’s farewell concert, Back to the Beginning, on July 5 in Birmingham, U.

item.title: MIKE PORTNOY Says LARS ULRICH Was a Major Influence: 'He Was More Than Just a Drummer'
item.description: Mike Portnoy, drummer for progressive metal band Dream Theater, recently shared that Lars Ulrich of Metallica had a big impact on his career, and not just behind the drum kit.

item.title: VENOM INC.'s TONY DOLAN Reacts To Public Accusations From MANTAS: 'They All Blame Me For Their Own Demise'
item.description: Tony Dolan is setting the record straight. The bassist and vocalist of VENOM INC. recently addressed his fallout with guitarist Jeff “Mantas” Dunn, who officially left the band in late 2023.

item.title: AC/DC Faces Backlash Over Viral Tour Footage As Fans Call For Retirement: 'Painful'
item.description: Footage from a recent AC/DC concert is making waves online, and not in the way the band might hope. A TikTok video from the group’s May 4 performance at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts, has gone viral (watch it below).

item.title: SEBASTIAN BACH Talks Dimebag Darrell’s Wild Hotel Incident: 'He Stabbed The Couch On Acid'
item.description: Sebastian Bach recently shared a wild story from his days on tour with Pantera. The former Skid Row frontman opened up in a new interview about a chaotic moment involving the late Dimebag Darrell, a knife, and a hotel lobby couch (via Sense Music Media) (transcribed by LOUDLEGENDS.

item.title: DAVID ELLEFSON Says DAVE MUSTAINE ‘Hated Playing Before SLAYER’ On 2010 Tour
item.description: Dave Mustaine wasn’t happy with his spot on the lineup during MEGADETH’s tours with SLAYER, according to former bandmate David Ellefson. In a recent episode of The David Ellefson Show podcast (transcribed by BLABBERMOUTH), the former MEGADETH bassist spoke about the 2010 Jägermeister Music Tour.

item.title: AARON STAINTHORPE Talks Leaving MY DYING BRIDE: 'I Feel 10 Years Younger'
item.description: Aaron Stainthorpe, known for fronting British metal band My Dying Bride for over three decades, says his new project has given him a fresh perspective, and a second wind.

item.title: Michael Paget Says BULLET FOR MY VALENTINE's New Album Will Feature 'Crazy Tuning'
item.description: Guitarist Michael “Padge” Paget says BULLET FOR MY VALENTINE is exploring new territory on their next studio album, including tunings the band has never used before. The longtime member of the Welsh metalcore group opened up about the upcoming record during a chat at this year’s Download Festival in the UK (watch the interview below).

item.title: KITTIE’s MORGAN LANDER Talks About Writing 'FIRE': 'It Was A Relearning Curve'
item.description: Getting back in the studio after more than a decade isn’t as simple as picking up where you left off. Just ask Morgan Lander. The guitarist and vocalist for Canadian metal band KITTIE says that writing Fire, their first album in 13 years, didn’t come with muscle memory (via TotalRock).

item.title: Dave 'PHOENIX' Farrell Talks LINKIN PARK’s Return: 'Time Doesn’t Heal The Wound, It Changes The Lens'
item.description: Linkin Park is back on tour with a new album and new members. But for bassist Dave “Phoenix” Farrell, returning to the band after Chester Bennington’s death was not easy.

item.title: Evanescence's AMY LEE Reflects On Pandemic-Era Lessons: 'Who Knows When This Will Ever End? So Let’s Put Out Our Music'
item.description: Amy Lee says the pandemic changed how Evanescence approaches releasing music. In a recent interview with WDHA-FM, the singer explained that waiting for a perfect moment to drop a full album no longer feels realistic.

item.title: AMY LEE Says New EVANESCENCE Album Coming 'Probably Early Next Year'
item.description: Evanescence is working on their next studio album, and according to Amy Lee, it’s likely to arrive in early 2026. The singer gave an update during a recent interview with WDHA-FM 105.

item.title: Dave 'PHOENIX' Farrell Breaks Silence on CHESTER BENNINGTON’s Death: 'Is It Even Called LINKIN PARK Anymore?'
item.description: Linkin Park bassist Dave “Phoenix” Farrell opened up about the band’s long road back to music after the loss of lead singer Chester Bennington. In a new interview with Czech station Evropa 2 (transcribed by BLABBERMOUTH.

item.title: Linkin Park’s EMILY ARMSTRONG Shaves Fan's Head on Stage at ROCK FOR PEOPLE 2025
item.description: Linkin Park opened their summer festival season with a big moment at Rock for People 2025. The band performed in front of 50,000 fans, but one person in the crowd definitely stood out.

item.title: Morgan Lander Says KITTIE May Release More Music: 'We’re Enjoying Ourselves'
item.description: KITTIE could be back in the studio again soon. Guitarist and vocalist Morgan Lander says the band is open to releasing more new music, thanks to the positive energy surrounding their recent reunion (transcribed by BLABBERMOUTH.

item.title: The Emotional METALLICA Song That Wasn’t Meant to Be, According to JAMES HETFIELD
item.description: When Load dropped in June 1996, it marked a sharp left turn for Metallica. The band traded speed and aggression for a slower, more reflective sound. That shift didn’t land well with everyone, but it did show fans a broader side of the band’s musical identity.

item.title: ASKING ALEXANDRIA Fans Question Danny Worsnop’s Performance, Call for His Exit
item.description: Asking Alexandria’s recent Warped Tour performance is stirring debate online, and some fans think it may be time for lead singer Danny Worsnop to step aside. The band’s subreddit lit up after their June 15 set, with over a dozen posts and hundreds of comments discussing Worsnop’s vocals and stage presence.

item.title: BULLET FOR MY VALENTINE's Michael Paget On New Album: 'It's Gonna Be Super Heavy'
item.description: BULLET FOR MY VALENTINE is working on new music, and according to guitarist Michael “Padge” Paget, fans should expect something heavier than ever before. The Welsh metal band recently cut its joint tour with Trivium short, choosing to focus instead on writing and recording their next studio album.

item.title: MEGADETH's DAVE MUSTAINE On the 'Puppy Incident': 'JAMES Got Punched In The Mouth. He Kicked My Dog'
item.description: There’s no elegant way to introduce a story that ends with James Hetfield catching a mouthful of knuckles. Especially when the instigating factor was a puppy. But here we are.

item.title: Ex-EXODUS RICK HUNOLT Looks Back On Thrash Origins: 'We Inspired METALLICA And SLAYER'
item.description: Ex-EXODUS guitarist Rick Hunolt didn’t bother dancing around it during a recent chat with Pod Scum host Rexx Ruger (transcribed by BLABBERMOUTH.NET). When Ruger put Hunolt and Gary Holt on the same tier as Hetfield/Hammett or Hanneman/King, Hunolt didn’t blink.

item.title: EUGENE ABDUKHANOV On MESHUGGAH's Early Days: 'People Didn’t Get It Then'
item.description: Eugene Abdukhanov isn’t new to giving credit where it’s due, even if it takes the rest of the world a couple of decades to catch up. Sitting down with Forever Loud at Download Festival, the JINJER bassist pulled no punches while looking back on what it was like watching MESHUGGAH rise from being the metal kid no one invited to the party, to becoming the very sound system (transcribed by BLABBERMOUTH.

item.title: STEVE DIGIORGIO On Recording With DAVE MUSTAINE: 'He Wasn't What I Expected'
item.description: Steve DiGiorgio, longtime bassist for Testament, has spoken candidly about his brief but intense experience recording with Dave Mustaine for Megadeth’s album The Sick, The Dying… And The Dead!

item.title: JAMES HETFIELD’s Favorite Thrash Bands (That Aren’t METALLICA, SLAYER, MEGADETH or ANTHRAX)
item.description: At this point, saying Metallica “isn’t thrash anymore” is like complaining MTV doesn’t play music videos. Welcome to the last three decades. Sure, the band traded speed for stadiums a while back, but try telling the IRS they’re not the face of thrash metal and see how that goes.

item.title: AMY LEE Talks About EMMA ANZAI Joining EVANESCENCE: 'I Called Her First'
item.description: Evanescence frontwoman Amy Lee has opened up about the band’s evolving lineup and her longtime connection with bassist Emma Anzai, offering rare insight into the decision-making behind the group’s most recent personnel shift.

item.title: FIT FOR A KING Announces New Album 'LONELY GOD', Shares Lead Single And Tracklist
item.description: Fit For A King have unveiled Lonely God, their eighth studio album, scheduled to arrive August 1, 2025 via Solid State Records. The announcement came with a music video (available at the end of this article) for the blistering title track, which showcases the band’s signature blend of gnarly riffs, guttural growls, heavy grooves, and a dash of industrial crunch.

item.title: Ex-Pantera TERRY GLAZE On DIMEBAG's Death: 'It Didn't Hit Me Until I Saw The Dirt'
item.description: Former Pantera vocalist Terry Glaze has shared a personal account of how he learned about the death of guitarist “Dimebag” Darrell Abbott and the emotional aftermath that followed.

item.title: PAUL STANLEY On KISS Reunion Regrets: 'Some Nights Were Awful'
item.description: Turns out the face paint couldn’t cover everything. Back in 2000, KISS slapped the word farewell on a tour, grabbed the original lineup, and hit the road like it was 1977 all over again.

item.title: AVENGED SEVENFOLD's M. SHADOWS On Being Misunderstood: 'People Are Just Getting It Now'
item.description: M. Shadows isn’t mad. He’s just… already moved on. If Life Is But a Dream… finally makes sense to you in 2025, congrats on solving the puzzle.

item.title: PIGGY D. On Working With MARILYN MANSON: 'I'm Proud To Stand Next To Him'
item.description: Matt Montgomery, better known as Piggy D., isn’t shy when it comes to describing his experience playing bass for Marilyn Manson. In a recent interview with Radioactive MikeZ on 96.

item.title: DAVE MUSTAINE Recalls METALLICA Audition: 'My Mom Used To Clean Lars' Apartment'
item.description: Dave Mustaine didn’t need to strike a single chord to sense the outcome of his audition for Metallica. After spotting their ad in a magazine, he reached out to Lars Ulrich and arranged to meet up in Newport Beach for a live tryout.

item.title: DUFF MCKAGAN Compares OZZY OSBOURNE to Lemmy, Prince, and Iggy Pop
item.description: Duff McKagan has seen plenty of rock stars come and go, but when it comes to Ozzy Osbourne, he doesn’t mince words. “A constant in rock and roll,” as he puts it.

item.title: MATT TUCK Says BULLET FOR MY VALENTINE Will Return To Studio: 'We Can't Wait To Drop New Music'
item.description: While stomping around Donington Park for the Download Festival in the UK, Matt Tuck finally offered something resembling an update on Bullet For My Valentine’s elusive eighth studio album.

item.title: DAVID VINCENT Reflects On Fan Expectations: 'Nobody Cares About The New Stuff'
item.description: David Vincent, the former Morbid Angel frontman, isn’t exactly rushing to crank out new material with I Am Morbid. In a recent sit-down with Altars Of Metal, the inevitable question popped up: will I Am Morbid ever release original songs?

item.title: Mike Portnoy Surprises Son Max With Dream Theater Drum Challenge at Drumeo
item.description: Max Portnoy walked into Drumeo expecting a normal day. Instead, his father, Mike Portnoy, waited for him with a surprise. Mike asked his son to play Honor Thy Father by Dream Theater without any practice.

item.title: James Hetfield Shares The Cost of Fame: ‘They Think They Know Me’
item.description: Metallica’s new documentary, Metallica Saved My Life, made its debut at the Tribeca Festival in New York City on June 11. After the screening, all four band members joined The New Yorker’s Amanda Petrusich for a conversation that pulled back the curtain on both their private lives and the inspiration behind the film.

item.title: Nirvana's "Smells Like Teen Spirit" Surpasses 2 Billion YouTube Views
item.description: Nirvana’s “Smells Like Teen Spirit” has now passed the 2-billion view mark on YouTube. After first being uploaded in 2009, the video quietly amassed its first billion by 2019.

item.title: David Ellefson Breaks Down Megadeth’s Risk and Its Divisive Legacy
item.description: In 1999, Megadeth rolled the dice with Risk, a record that veered sharply away from the band’s thrash metal identity. For David Ellefson, the album remains, in his own words, “probably the most controversial album in the catalog.

item.title: Motörhead Releases 'Leavin’ Here' Video From Recently Discovered 1976 Tapes
item.description: After nearly five decades of dust, decay, and general disregard, Motörhead has cracked open the time capsule no one saw coming. The band has just dropped a music video for “Leavin’ Here”, a snarling slab of rock that also happens to be one of the oldest recordings from the Lemmy–Eddie Clarke–Phil Taylor era.

item.title: Inside Halestorm’s Risky Recording Process for New Album Everest
item.description: Halestorm walked into Everest with a backpack full of unfinished songs. Turns out, producer Dave Cobb didn’t want any of it. “We’re not doing demos. I hate demos,” he told them.

item.title: KILLSWITCH ENGAGE Shares Music Video For 'Collusion' Single From 'This Consequence' Album
item.description: Killswitch Engage is back with This Consequence, their ninth studio album, and they’ve just unleashed a music video for the track “Collusion”, which, spoiler alert, is NOT about happy things.

item.title: Vogg Says Decapitated’s New Album is Halfway Done, But When Will It Drop?
item.description: OKAY, SO—Vogg, the guitar wizard of Decapitated, has somehow managed to write 50% of the band’s new album. Fifty. Percent. Not 49%. Not 51%. Exactly half. And he dropped this information like it was no big deal while floating on the 70000 Tons of Metal cruise, which, if you don’t know, is basically a lawless, floating metal festival where dehydration, questionable decisions, and ear-shattering riffs collide on the high seas.

item.title: Dream Theater’s Mike Portnoy on Pain, Perseverance, and Playing Through Injury
item.description: Step into this scene with me… Dream Theater, mid-’90s, prog-metal gods playing Awake on tour—Portnoy’s behind the kit, hair flailing, sticks a blur, sweat dripping like he’s trying to personally refill the Dead Sea.

item.title: Zakk Wylde’s Black Label Society Drops 'Lord Humungus'—New Single Out Now
item.description: you ever hear a song so ridiculously heavy it makes you wanna run through a wall—like, FULL Kool-Aid Man mode—except the wall is made of steel and your doctor is already tired of your bullshit?

item.title: Killswitch Engage’s Mike D’Antonio Rejects A.I. Claims: "I Don’t Wanna Be Associated With It"
item.description: Another day, another internet conspiracy theory—this time, aimed at Killswitch Engage bassist and graphic designer Mike D’Antonio, who’s had to crawl out of the art cave he’s been living in for the past eight months just to tell people to shut the hell up about A.

item.title: AVANTASIA’s 'Here Be Dragons' Features KAMELOT’s Tommy Karevik on New Single The Witch
item.description: Well, folks, let me tell ya’ll, Tobias Sammet is back with another Avantasia album, and this time he’s gone full medieval cartographer on us. The tenth studio album, Here Be Dragons, is set to release on February 28, 2025, via Napalm Records, and based on everything we know, it’s shaping up to be either a symphonic masterpiece or the musical equivalent of a Renaissance Fair gone horribly wrong.

item.title: Arch Enemy's Alissa White-Gluz Joins Savage Lands on New Single “Ruling Queen”
item.description: I knew a guy once—swore on his mother’s grave that trees could scream. Not metaphorically, not some poetic nonsense about deforestation being a “cry for help.” No, he meant it literally, said he heard it with his own ears—a deep, resonant moan every time an axe struck bark.

item.title: Arch Enemy Drops "Paper Tiger" Music Video and Reveals Blood Dynasty Tour Dates
item.description: Ok SO listen—Arch Enemy decided that the world needed to be LOUDER, and who are we to argue??? They dropped “Paper Tiger” and I swear to Odin’s beard it’s got that Judas Priest but also Arch Enemy but also maybe a bit of an angry chainsaw vibe.

item.title: Meshuggah Drops "Ligature Marks" Music Video Alongside "Immutable - The Indelible Edition" Announcement
item.description: Yep, MESHUGGAH is back to make your speakers beg for mercy—again. Not just playing their usual brand of mind-melting, time-signature-abusing, existential-crisis-inducing metal—oh no, they’ve decided to remaster their already ridiculous 2022 album Immutable and slap on a shiny new title: “Immutable - The Indelible Edition” (because clearly, “Immutable” wasn’t immutable enough).

item.title: SPIRITBOX Releases "No Loss, No Love" Ahead of "Tsunami Sea" Album Drop; VIDEO
item.description: SPIRITBOX did what now? Dropped a new single? No Loss, No Love? A chaotic, genre-hopping, existential crisis in song form? Yeah, that checks out. This band is out here treating musical boundaries like a cheap piñata, just smashing them apart, stuffing the remains with eerie atmospherics and whatever the hell Courtney LaPlante feels like doing with her voice that day.

item.title: Lorraine Lewis on Joining OnlyFans: "It’s Sexy, I’m Owning It, And I’m Having Fun!"
item.description: Lorraine Lewis. 66 years old. Rock icon. Ex-VIXEN. Current FEMME FATALE badass. Also? Now officially on OnlyFans. And not just dipping her toes in—she’s fully in the pool.

item.title: Stray From The Path Releases “Kubrick Stare” – A New Single Under SharpTone Records; VIDEO
item.description: Stray From The Path is back. And they’re bringing paranoia with them. Their latest single, “Kubrick Stare”, just dropped (February 5, 2025, mark it) with a music video that’s—well, unsettling, in the best way.

item.title: Max Cavalera on Re-Recording SEPULTURA’s Early Albums: “They Never Sounded Right”
item.description: Oh boy, here we go. Another “let’s redo our old stuff, but this time better” kind of deal. You know, like when you rewrite a high school essay as an adult and suddenly realize, wow, I really didn’t understand metaphors back then.

item.title: Sharon den Adel Confirms Within Temptation’s Next Album Is Taking Shape: “We Have a Clear Vision”
item.description: So Within Temptation has a plan. Well, sort of. Sharon den Adel insists they “really have an idea what we wanna do next,” which sounds promising—until you realize that the band started with the intention of taking their sweet time, only to immediately flip-flop.

item.title: Watch: Marty Friedman Drops Visualizer for “A Prayer” From Drama
item.description: Marty Friedman, the once-and-forever legendary (but now solo and doing his thing) former MEGADETH guitarist, just threw a visualizer our way for his track “A Prayer.” You know, that song from his album Drama?

item.title: OnlyFans and Rock: Lorraine Lewis, The FEMME FATALE singer, embraces her wild side with new content
item.description: Lorraine Lewis isn’t just standing still. She’s moving, shaking things up, and dragging rock and roll with her (kicking and screaming, probably). You remember her, right? The voice behind FEMME FATALE.

item.title: Michael Wilton Talks New Queensrÿche Album and 2025 Goals
item.description: Queensrÿche guitarist Michael Wilton spoke with Robert Cavuoto (for MyGlobalMind). Touched on new record plans? Absolutely. Also reflected on the many twists and turns the band has faced over the decades (and there have been plenty).

item.title: Necrobutcher on Mayhem's Four Decades of Survival
item.description: When the bassist of your band murders the guitarist, you’d think the group might call it quits. Most bands implode over petty squabbles about songwriting credits or tour schedules—not criminal trials.

item.title: Ryan McCombs Wishes Social Media Never Existed—But He Still Uses It
item.description: Ryan McCombs—frontman of Drowning Pool and SOIL, master of growls, occasional philosopher—has thoughts about social media. Big ones. Messy ones. The kind that make you nod along until he throws in a time-travel fantasy about stopping Zuckerberg in his tracks (we’ll get there).

item.title: Why Tommy Lee Showers Once a Week, According to His Wife
item.description: Tommy Lee, drummer for Mötley Crüe, bathes sparingly. His wife, Brittany Furlan, says he showers only once a week. The detail emerged on Kaitlyn Bristowe’s Off the Vine podcast, where Furlan spoke about her husband’s habits.

item.title: Watch: RAMMSTEIN Shares Exclusive Tour Documentary; VIDEO
item.description: RAMMSTEIN’s World Stadium Tour 2019–2024 documentary is here, clocking in at just under an hour. For a band that’s made an entire career out of fire, leather, and eyebrow-scorching theatrics, they’ve now decided to show us the real magic—spoiler alert: it’s the crew hauling stage pieces like they’re building the pyramids.

item.title: KISS Icon Gene Simmons Speaks Out on Reagan Movie Controversy
item.description: Gene Simmons—yes, the man with the tongue, the fire-breathing antics, and more merchandise than a small country—has added movie soundtrack contributor to his résumé. Recently, he recorded a cover of “Stormy Weather” for the biopic Reagan.

item.title: NIGHTWISH Goes Behind-the-Scenes with 'Yesterwynde' Doc; VIDEO
item.description: NIGHTWISH, the masters of symphonic bombast, have dropped a 45-minute documentary that peels back the layers of their latest opus, “Yesterwynde.” Released on September 20, this album wraps up the trilogy that kicked off with “Endless Forms Most Beautiful” in 2015.

item.title: Linkin Park’s Mike Shinoda: “Our New Lineup Came Together Naturally”
item.description: Linkin Park is back. New album (listen below). New lineup. Same vibe. This one’s called “From Zero”, which feels like a bit of an oversell for a band that’s been rehashing itself since 2017.

item.title: Linkin Park’s Mike Shinoda Talks Brad Delson’s Tour Absence
item.description: Linkin Park’s reunion, complete with a fresh album release last Friday, has been making waves. Yet, the band’s current lineup feels like a revolving door. With Chester Bennington’s tragic loss in 2017 and drummer Rob Bourdon sitting this one out, it’s already a scaled-back return.

item.title: Mike Shinoda on Why Brad Delson Isn’t Touring With Linkin Park
item.description: Brad Delson, the longtime six-string maestro of Linkin Park, is still very much part of the band. In the studio, behind the scenes—he’s there, making things happen. But if you were hoping to see him shred live, prepare for disappointment.

item.title: The Surprise You Missed in Korn’s 1997 Track "A.D.I.D.A.S."
item.description: Ever really listened to the breakdown in Korn’s 1997 track “A.D.I.D.A.S.”? And I mean actually listened—ears glued to every sound, every tiny layer. There’s a surprise in there you probably missed.

item.title: Watch: Korn Celebrates 30 Years with Epic Anniversary Concert in Los Angeles
item.description: Nu metal’s elder statesmen, Korn, threw a massive party this past weekend in Los Angeles. Their 30th Anniversary bash at BMO Stadium was less of a concert and more of a nu metal reunion, complete with thousands of fans who still remember when baggy jeans and wallet chains were a statement.

item.title: Watch: DREAM THEATER Releases 'Night Terror' Video Ahead of 'Parasomnia' Album
item.description: February 7, 2025, marks the arrival of DREAM THEATER’s sixteenth album, “Parasomnia,” via InsideOut Music. This time, they’ve reunited with their prodigal son, drummer Mike Portnoy, whose last contribution to the band dates back to 2009’s “Black Clouds & Silver Linings.

item.title: Shavo Odadjian’s Seven Hours After Violet Drops New Single "Cry"; VIDEO
item.description: Shavo Odadjian is back with his new project—SEVEN HOURS AFTER VIOLET—and they’ve just dropped the music video for their latest single, “Cry.” Far from being a System of a Down copycat, this track goes straight into anguish, longing, and all the good ol’ despair you’d expect from a song called “Cry.

item.title: As I Lay Dying Previews 'Through Storms Ahead' With New Single; VIDEO
item.description: As I Lay Dying has rolled out their latest offering, “Whitewashed Tomb,” a mid-tempo track that gives a preview of their upcoming album, Through Storms Ahead, slated for release on November 15.

item.title: SKILLET's John Cooper on Political Divides in Rock: "We're Shut Out"
item.description: In a recent chat with the Rebellious Remarks podcast, John Cooper, frontman for SKILLET, took the opportunity to drop some of his usual truth bombs about being a Christian rock musician in today’s ultra-polarized world.

item.title: Ted Nugent Praises Metallica’s "Soulful" Groove While Criticizing Pantera
item.description: In a recent episode of Ted Nugent’s show “Spirit Campfire” on Real America’s Voice, the ever-outspoken Nugent threw a nod to several rockers who are still out there tearing up stages, mentioning Mark Farner, STYX, and Sammy Hagar as some of the enduring performers.

item.title: Watch: Linkin Park Partners with Riot Games for League of Legends Anthem
item.description: Linkin Park is back, boys and girls. Again. This time, they’ve teamed up with Riot Games for “Heavy Is The Crown,” the official anthem for the League of Legends 2024 World Championship.

item.title: 'Master Of Puppets' Wins Out for Shavo Odadjian in METALLICA Album Showdown
item.description: When Shavo Odadjian, bassist of SYSTEM OF A DOWN, got hit with the impossible question of whether METALLICA’s “Ride The Lightning” or “Master Of Puppets” was the superior album during an interview with Radioactive MikeZ on 96.

item.title: Watch: New Sound, New Faces: Linkin Park Rocks Jimmy Fallon; VIDEO
item.description: Linkin Park hit Jimmy Fallon’s stage last night (17) with their new single, “The Emptiness Machine.” If you missed it, don’t worry. It’s online, complete with enough fog to choke a small village.

item.title: Watch: Korn Performs "Hey Daddy" Live for First Time Since 1999
item.description: Korn pulled a fast one last night. “Hey Daddy”—yep, that’s right. Played live for the first time since 1999. This wasn’t just a random throwback either. September 12, Tampa, Florida.

item.title: Korn Kicks Off 2024 Tour with a Nostalgic Setlist in Tampa
item.description: Korn’s North American tour kicked off last night, and for those of us who’ve been around long enough to remember them actually playing these songs when they first dropped, it was a bit of a nostalgia trip—whether we asked for it or not.

item.title: As I Lay Dying: 'We Are The Dead' Drops with Alex Terrible and Tom Barber; VIDEO
item.description: As I Lay Dying is gearing up to drop their latest album, Through Storms Ahead, set to land on November 15. Nestled among the tracks are “Burden,” “The Cave We Fear to Enter,” and the freshly unleashed “We Are The Dead.

item.title: Watch: Mushroomhead Fans Clash with Slipknot in 1999 Show
item.description: Back in 1999, the tension between Slipknot and Mushroomhead wasn’t just gossip, it was a full-on warzone. A recently resurfaced video from a Cleveland Slipknot show captures this beautiful disaster in all its chaotic glory.

item.title: Slipknot’s 25th Anniversary Kicks Off with Nothing After 1999; VIDEO
item.description: Slipknot has been teasing this nostalgia-heavy tour for what feels like forever, and last night in Noblesville, Indiana, they finally unleashed the beast. Their ‘Here Comes the Pain Tour’ is officially underway, celebrating 25 years of their self-titled debut—a record that pretty much defined what it meant to be an angry, sweaty teenager in the late ’90s.

item.title: Phil Labonte: Korn’s Impact on Deathcore Goes Beyond Nu-Metal
item.description: When a band ends up becoming so influential that people start crediting them for launching a whole subgenre, it’s something to take note of. But when a group gets blamed for a genre they don’t even directly belong to?

item.title: As I Lay Dying Drops Emotional New Track, "The Cave We Fear to Enter"; VIDEO
item.description: Looks like As I Lay Dying has decided to venture into metaphorical spelunking. Their latest single, “The Cave We Fear to Enter,” leans heavily into clean vocals and was born out of an idea from bassist and vocalist Ryan Neff.

item.title: Watch: As I Lay Dying Is Back: 'Burden' Released, Tour Announced
item.description: As I Lay Dying has returned with “Burden”, their first new single in five years, featuring their revamped lineup. The track introduces Ken Susi (ex-Unearth), Nick Pierce (ex-Unearth), and Ryan Neff (Miss May I), marking a new chapter for the band.

item.title: Slipknot Revives 1999 Look at Intimate Anniversary Show; VIDEO
item.description: In a tiny California venue better suited for a rowdy karaoke night than the launch of a metal juggernaut’s 25th anniversary, Slipknot made a dramatic entrance. Decked out in those bright red jumpsuits that defined their early days, the band treated the packed crowd at Pappy + Harriet’s in Pioneertown to a full-on blast from the past.

item.title: Linkin Park Rumored to Return with a Female Lead Singer
item.description: July marks seven years since Chester Bennington’s untimely passing—a moment that shattered not just his family and friends, but the entire world of Linkin Park fans. His death wasn’t just tragic; it was a full stop.

item.title: Linkin Park Releases "Friendly Fire" Featuring Chester Bennington
item.description: Art has a way of keeping artists alive, doesn’t it? Even when they’re gone, their work lingers on, creating an odd form of immortality. Linkin Park just gave fans a bittersweet reminder of that idea by releasing “Friendly Fire”, an unreleased track featuring the unmistakable vocals of the late Chester Bennington.

item.title: Watch: Korn Meets Vanessa Carlton in a Bizarre Mashup
item.description: Just when you thought the world had run out of odd musical combinations, along comes YouTuber mac glocky with a new creation. Fresh off his last “masterpiece”—a mashup of System of a Down and the B-52s—he’s back with another experiment: what happens when you blend Vanessa Carlton’s early 2000s pop hit “A Thousand Miles” with the nu-metal force of Korn?

item.title: Korn's Brian Welch Introduces New Record Label XOVR Records; VIDEO
item.description: Brian “Head” Welch, the guitarist from Korn, has decided that making loud noises on stage wasn’t quite enough, so he’s now entering the record label world with his latest venture, XOVR Records (that’s “Crossover Records” for those who don’t speak in mysterious abbreviations).

item.title: Watch: Metallica Drops New “Too Far Gone?” Video with Tour Highlights
item.description: Metallica might’ve dropped 72 Seasons a mere five months back, but the internet reaction could’ve fooled anyone into thinking it’s been years since that release. One side hollered about “disastrous trash,” while the other shrugged, calling it “pretty decent.

item.title: Watch: Exclusive Footage of Metallica's Phantom Lord from Jon Zazula Tribute
item.description: Metallica just dropped official footage of them ripping through Phantom Lord at last weekend’s tribute show for their old manager, Jon Zazula. Yeah, it was one of those nights.

item.title: Watch: Metallica Pays Tribute to Megaforce Founders with Old-School Set
item.description: Metallica recently gave fans a nostalgic kick in the gut with a special throwback show that would make any old-school fan tear up—if they’re still capable of crying, that is.
